correctness.rationale: For every fixed n≥3 and C² strictly convex K with positive curvature, h+h″ is the correct arclength Jacobian. The missing-semicircle integral exactly characterizes boundedness. Solving consecutive tangent lines gives q=w v/δ+O(1) as a single angular gap g=π−δ approaches π; two oriented shoelace terms contribute w²/(2δ). The support-height perimeter identity bounds A by a constant times the sum of (π−g_i)^{-1}. A joint simplex-volume bound suppresses multiple gaps near π. The exact adjacent-pair intensity then gives the stated integral constant, strictly positive and finite. The t^{-1} tail implies the moment threshold. Closed Fourier identities and finite computational checks agree, but the computations are not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The identified contribution is the curvature/antipodal-width functional for the *fixed-n conditional large-area tail* of arbitrary C² positively curved bodies and arbitrary positive normal densities, with an exact constant-width separation example. The known unit-circle formula is a special case and is not asserted original. Fodor–Hug–Ziebarth instead study n→∞ truncated random half-space intersections; their full primary preprint was read in its theorem/model sections. Xu 2015 studies random tangent polygons of a circle; an accessible abstract, not the complete text, was available. No inspected source implies the arbitrary-curve coefficient or constant-width distinction. The unresolved historical coverage risk from inaccessible Xu full text is recorded.

value.rationale: The area of a random polygon circumscribing a convex body is a canonical approximation functional. Its finite-sample tail conditional on actual boundedness is a natural previously unquantified obstruction, not a formal normalization check. The result supplies a complete universal exponent, a geometric leading constant coupling antipodal curvature density, complementary semicircle mass, and squared width, plus a sharp integrability boundary for every n. The explicit noncircular constant-width family shows that the tail captures information not determined by width, giving the precise invariant mathematical motivation and a concrete comparison class.
